terms.grammar: imperative of caveō: alone; with an accusative (cavē canem); with nē and the subjunctive, or the bare subjunctive (cavē cadās); plural cavēte
evidence: Plaut. Most. 324b: Cavē nē cadās, astā.
terms.comment: In comedy often with sīs (“mind, will you”). In Plautus’ verse the final vowel is often shortened in speech (cave); the word is cavē.

terms.gloss: look out for yourself! mind out!

evidence: Hor. S. 1.4.85: hic niger est, hunc tū, Rōmāne, cavētō
terms.comment: The future imperative of rules and warnings that hold from now on.
Cavē with a bare subjunctive forbids (cavē quisquam floccī fēcerit, Plaut. Men. 5.7.5, Lewis & Short s.v. caveō), so this says “don’t look around”. Say Circumspice! or Cavē!.

phrases.latin: canis ingēns, catēnā vīnctus, in pariete erat pictus superque quadrātā litterā scrīptum CAVĒ CANEM
phrases.english: a huge dog on a chain was painted on the wall, and above it in capitals BEWARE OF THE DOG
Careful you don’t fall; stand still.
Mind you don’t get into trouble.

phrases.latin: hic niger est, hunc tū, Rōmāne, cavētō
phrases.english: he is a black heart: Roman, beware of him
